verdict.rationale: Pipecat is a code-first voice-agent framework. The evidence shows developer event hooks (turn events for collecting messages, client SDK events) and built-in behaviors like barge-in interruption, but no product feature for defining event-triggered automation rules. These are developer building blocks or fixed behaviors, not a user-definable rules capability, so they earn no credit. The axis is fair for a framework or cloud platform of this kind, so absence of evidence is none rather than na.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Pipecat's turn events make it easy to collect both user and assistant messages as they occur.
provide messaging and events for building responsive voice AI interfaces
